no hype. Use only the provided material; every number must appear in it. When you name the source of a number,

response: {"headline": "ILLUMINATE (torcetrapib) was stopped for harm on 2006-12-02 after the DSMB found an imbalance of mortality and cardiovascular events, driven by an off-target blood pressure elevation not shared by other CETP inhibitors.", "summary": "The ILLUMINATE trial randomized 15,067 patients with established cardiovascular disease and low HDL-C (men <44 mg/dl; women <54 mg/dl) to torcetrapib 60 mg QD plus atorvastatin versus atorvastatin alone, with time to first major cardiovascular event as the primary endpoint. The independent DSMB recommended terminating the study because of an imbalance of mortality and cardiovascular events. Phase 2 data had shown small increases in systolic and diastolic blood pressure, with significant BP increases in 2 of 140 subjects. The calculator, operating in forecast mode with unknown follow-up and event count, returned not_computable (category insufficient_data) and predicted only a 9% RRR (HR 0.91) based on an assumed LDL-C baseline of 2.0 mmol/L and -18.9% LDL-C lowering at 90 mg/day, requiring 3,560 events for 80% power. The fundamental weaknesses were HDL-C non-causality (the drug class was developed to raise HDL-C, which is classified as non-causal for coronary disease) and absent pre-cutoff CETP genetic evidence (Open Targets score 0.736 but evidence_before_cutoff = 0). The observed harm — opposite to the predicted benefit — confirms off-target toxicity (aldosterone/BP elevation) specific to torcetrapib.", "key_evidence": ["15,067 participants randomized (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00134264 ILLUMINATE)", "Primary endpoint: time to first major cardiovascular disease event (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00134264 ILLUMINATE)", "DSMB recommended terminating due to imbalance of mortality and CV events (Pfizer press release Dec 2, 2006)", "Small increases in systolic and diastolic blood pressures noted in phase 2 (Efficacy and safety of torcetrapib... on background of atorvastatin)", "Significant BP increases in 2 of 140 subjects (Efficacy and safety of torcetrapib... in individuals with below-average HDL-C)", "HDL-C increase 40.2% placebo-adjusted at 90 mg/day on atorvastatin background (Efficacy and safety of torcetrapib... on background of atorvastatin)", "HDL-C increases up to 382% across phase 2 studies (multiple sources)", "LDL-C decrease -18.9% at 90 mg/day on atorvastatin background (Efficacy and safety of torcetrapib... on background of atorvastatin)", "LDL-C decrease -22.2% in phase 2 (Efficacy and safety of torcetrapib... in individuals with below-average HDL-C)", "Calculator: expected HR 0.91, causal RRR 9%, category insufficient_data, weakest_link target genetics: not_causal (calculator)", "Calculator assumptions: LDL-C baseline assumed 2.0, follow-up unknown, events needed for 80% power: 3,560 (calculator)", "Open Targets CETP genetic association score 0.736 (opentargets:CETP)"], "what_would_change_this": "The trial was stopped for definitive harm; nothing would reverse that outcome. Earlier recognition of the off-target blood pressure/aldosterone signal in phase 2 might have prevented the phase 3 launch or prompted dose de-escalation.", "readthrough_note": "Other CETP inhibitors (dalcetrapib, anacetrapib, evacetrapib) were in development; anacetrapib (REVEAL) later showed neutral cardiovascular outcomes without the blood pressure harm, confirming the toxicity was off-target to torcetrapib, not a class effect of CETP inhibition."}
